title: Fulbright Foreign Student Program
provider: U.S. Department of State (Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs)
description: Flagship U.S. government exchange programme funding master's and doctoral study or research at U.S. universities for graduate students, young professionals and artists from more than 160 countries. Applications are managed by the binational Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy in each home country.
amount: Full tuition, living stipend, airfare, health insurance

title: Knight-Hennessy Scholars
description: Fully funded graduate fellowship covering any full-time graduate degree at Stanford (MA, MS, MBA, JD, MD, PhD and others), paired with a leadership development programme. Open to applicants of any nationality; candidates apply separately to a Stanford graduate programme.
amount: Full tuition, living and academic stipend, travel allowance

title: Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program
field: Public policy, development, public health, agriculture, law, education, journalism
description: Non-degree fellowship bringing experienced mid-career professionals from designated countries to the United States for one year of graduate-level study and professional development. Administered through binational Fulbright Commissions and U.S. Embassies.
amount: Full programme costs, monthly stipend, airfare, health coverage, professional allowances

title: AAUW International Fellowships
description: Fellowships for women who are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents, supporting full-time master's, doctoral or postdoctoral study and research in the United States. Recipients are expected to return to their home country to pursue a professional career.

title: Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme
description: Need-based scholarships for outstanding students from selected developing countries who have no other means of financing their graduate studies, including at universities in the United States. Awarded as 50% grant and 50% loan.
amount: Tuition plus living expenses (50% grant, 50% interest-free loan)

title: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship Program
description: Scholarships for citizens of World Bank member developing countries to pursue a development-related master's degree at designated universities, several of which are in the United States. Applicants need at least three years of development-related work experience.
amount: Full tuition, monthly living stipend, airfare, health insurance

title: P.E.O. International Peace Scholarship
description: Scholarship for selected women from outside the United States and Canada pursuing graduate study at institutions in the U.S. or Canada. Applicants must be within one year of completing their programme and demonstrate financial need.

title: Margaret McNamara Education Grants (MMEG)
description: Grants for women from developing countries who are enrolled at an accredited U.S. or Canadian institution, are at least 25 years old, and are committed to improving the lives of women and children in their home country.

title: Emerging Global Leader Scholarship (AU EGLS)
description: Highly selective award for incoming international first-year undergraduate students who intend to return to their home country to effect positive change in an underserved community. Covers the full cost of attendance for one student and offers partial awards to others.
amount: Full tuition, room and board (one award); partial awards up to USD 40,000 per year

title: Cornell University Tata Scholarship
description: Need-based scholarship funded by the Tata Education and Development Trust for undergraduate students who are citizens of India and require financial aid to attend Cornell. Up to 20 students are supported at any one time.
amount: Financial aid covering demonstrated need (tuition and living costs)
